before.title: Alternator Failure from Age and Oil Contamination Leading to Charging Loss
before.description: First-generation IS300s commonly experience alternator failure as mileage climbs, sometimes accelerated by nearby oil leaks contaminating the unit. Owners report battery warning lights, dimming lights, low system voltage, and stalling after the battery discharges. Because the car may continue running briefly on battery power, the problem is sometimes mistaken for a bad battery alone.
before.solution: Test charging voltage at idle and under load, and inspect for oil leakage from the valve cover or power steering area that may have reached the alternator. Replace the alternator with a quality OEM or Denso unit and correct any fluid leaks that contributed to failure. The battery should be load-tested afterward because repeated deep discharge can damage it.

communityRecommendations.content: Owners frequently recommend Denso/OEM alternators over low-cost reman units because cheaper replacements often have short service life.
Fix valve cover leaks before installing a new alternator so the replacement is not contaminated.

proposal.title: Alternator Failure from Age and Oil Contamination Leading to Charging Loss
proposal.description: The complete federal communication inventory for the 2001-2005 IS 300 contains no exact record establishing a recurring alternator failure pattern, oil-contamination mechanism, common mileage range, or confusion with battery failure. The page currently provides no citation, measured field population, diagnostic threshold, or verified Denso application.
proposal.solution: Treat a battery warning lamp, low voltage or stalling as a charging-system diagnosis, not automatic proof of an alternator failure. A qualified technician should test battery condition, charging output, cable voltage drop and any fluid leak before replacing a component. This is a vehicle-specific diagnostic/service remedy; no universal retail part is asserted.
proposal.contentUpdateSummary: Removed the unsupported common-failure, oil-contamination and Denso-replacement claims; held the indexed identity for exact first-generation evidence.

before.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (2.0T)
before.description: The direct-injected 2.0L turbo four-cylinder in the IS200t/IS300 accumulates heavy carbon deposits on the intake valves since fuel is not sprayed over the valves to clean them. This leads to rough idle, hesitation under acceleration, and reduced power output typically between 40,000-80,000 miles.
before.solution: Perform a walnut shell blasting of the intake valves to remove carbon deposits. This requires removing the intake manifold and using specialized media blasting equipment. Plan to repeat every 40,000-60,000 miles. Using a quality catch can helps slow the buildup rate.
symptoms: Reduced power and sluggish throttle response
Slight misfire feel at low RPM

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — IS200t/IS300 carbon buildup walnut blasting guide and interval recommendations

communityRecommendations.content: JLT Performance oil catch can — catches oil vapor before it reaches the intake valves, significantly reducing carbon buildup between walnut blasting services.

proposal.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves (2.0T)
proposal.description: The complete IS-family communication inventory contains no exact Lexus record establishing heavy intake-valve carbon as a recurring 2016-2022 8AR-FTS defect, a 40,000-80,000-mile onset, or a repeat service interval. proposal.solution: Do not schedule walnut blasting or install a catch can from this page. Diagnose rough idle, hesitation or reduced power with codes, fuel trims, ignition checks and model-specific Lexus procedures before inspecting intake deposits or authorizing cleaning. This is a vehicle-specific diagnostic/service remedy; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface
before.description: The IS dashboard develops a sticky, melting surface identical to the ES and GS models of the same era. The dashboard material breaks down chemically in heat and sun exposure, creating a reflective glare on the windshield and a tacky feel. Lexus extended warranty coverage through Customer Support Program ZE7.
before.solution: Obtain dashboard replacement under the Lexus Customer Support Program ZE7 extended warranty. If coverage has expired, request goodwill assistance from Lexus corporate. Aftermarket dash covers provide a temporary cosmetic fix but do not resolve the underlying material breakdown.
symptoms: Dashboard surface becomes sticky and tacky
Chemical odor from dashboard in heat

citations.title: NHTSA complaint cluster — Lexus IS dashboard melting defect affecting 2006-2013 models

communityRecommendations.content: Even if you are past the official warranty extension, Lexus customer support has authorized free dashboard replacements on a case-by-case basis. Call 1-800-255-3987 and be persistent.

proposal.title: Dashboard Melting and Sticky Surface

proposal.solution: Do not promise ZE7 coverage, a free dashboard, or goodwill assistance from this page. Have a Lexus dealer identify the VIN, production period and any historical ZLD/ZLZ record, then obtain a current paid-repair estimate if no open coverage remains. before.title: Front Door Trim / Inner Garnish Rattle at Speaker Area
before.description: Multiple owners of current-generation Lexus IS models report a persistent rattle or buzzing from the front door panel area, often near the speaker grille or inner garnish, especially on rough pavement or with bass-heavy audio. Lexus issued service guidance for door trim noise on this generation, indicating the condition is known at the dealer level. Owners typically describe the noise as intermittent at first, then easier to reproduce as clips, felt interfaces, or trim contact points loosen slightly.
before.solution: Technicians usually road-test the vehicle to isolate the exact door and trim contact point, then remove the affected door panel and apply anti-rattle felt, foam tape, or updated insulators at the speaker grille, garnish, or clip interfaces. Broken or loose retaining clips should be replaced, and the panel should be reinstalled with proper torque and alignment. If the noise is audio-induced, verify the speaker fasteners and harness routing before reassembly.
symptoms: Buzzing or rattling from front door panel
Noise over bumps or rough roads
Intermittent trim noise near speaker grille

communityRecommendations.content: Before dealer visit, reproduce the noise with bass-heavy audio and note which door and road surface triggers it most consistently.
If DIY-inspecting, check door panel clips and speaker fasteners first; loose clips are a common source of intermittent buzzes.

before.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Failure (Recall)
before.description: The low-pressure fuel pump impeller can deform due to excessive fuel absorption, causing the fuel pump to become inoperative. This results in engine stalling while driving or inability to start, creating a serious safety hazard. Toyota/Lexus issued a massive recall (20V-863) affecting over 1.8 million vehicles across multiple models.
before.solution: Replace the fuel pump assembly at any Lexus dealer free of charge under recall 20V-863. The dealer replaces the entire fuel pump with an updated unit that uses a redesigned impeller. If you have not received a recall notice, contact your dealer with your VIN to verify eligibility.
symptoms: Engine stalls while driving without warning
Engine runs rough or sputters at speed

citations.title: NHTSA: Toyota Motor North America 20V-012 Denso Fuel Pump Recall
ClassAction.org: Jan. 2020 Toyota, Lexus Denso Fuel Pump Recall Left Out 2018-2019 Vehicles
ToyotaNation: Toyotas fuel pump recall list thus far

communityRecommendations.content: This is a safety recall — do not delay getting the fuel pump replaced. Engine stalling at highway speed has caused multiple accidents. Check NHTSA.gov with your VIN for recall status.

proposal.title: Fuel Pump Impeller Failure (Recall)
proposal.description: Toyota’s amended 20V-012 report and Lexus 20LA01 notice document low-pressure fuel pumps whose impellers may deform after fuel absorption and stop operating, creating rough running, no-start or stall risk. The exact Lexus IS applicability shown in the primary records is 2017 IS 200t, 2018-2019 IS 300, and 2014-2015/2018-2019 IS 350, with 20V-682 expanding the population. The page’s 20V-863 number and universal 2018-2020 IS 300/350 scope are incorrect; only VIN-listed vehicles are included.
proposal.solution: Check the full VIN in the official Lexus/NHTSA recall lookup for campaign 20LA01 (NHTSA 20V-012 or 20V-682). An authorized Lexus dealer replaces the low-pressure fuel pump with the recall remedy at no charge when the VIN has an open campaign. Do not buy a pump from a model-year list alone. This is a VIN-specific dealer recall remedy; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: LCD Climate Control and Radio Display Pixel Failure
before.description: The factory climate/audio display in the first-gen IS is known for dimming, losing pixels, or becoming unreadable with age. Owners report missing segments, blank screens, and difficulty adjusting HVAC settings at night or in bright daylight. This is a very common age-related electronics issue on 2001-2005 cars.
before.solution: Verify the issue is in the display unit rather than a fuse or backlighting power supply. Repair options include sending the unit to a specialist for LCD/pixel repair, replacing the display assembly with a known-good unit, or converting to an aftermarket audio/HVAC solution where applicable. Used units can fail the same way, so rebuilt parts are often preferred.

citations.title: My.IS and ClubLexus threads documenting IS300 climate/radio display pixel failures

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often prefer specialist rebuild services over salvage-yard replacements because rebuilt units typically address the underlying display failure.
Take photos of connector positions before removing the center stack to avoid reassembly mistakes.

before.title: Lexus Safety System+ False Forward Collision / PCS Warnings from Dirty or Misaligned Sensors
before.description: Some owners report intermittent pre-collision system, radar cruise, or lane-support warnings on 2023-2025 Lexus IS models, often after heavy rain, road grime buildup, windshield contamination, or minor front-end impacts. The system may temporarily disable with a message indicating the camera or radar is unavailable, even though no permanent hardware failure exists. In other cases, sensor alignment or calibration drift after windshield or bumper work can trigger recurring warnings.
before.solution: Inspect and clean the front radar emblem area and windshield camera zone first, then scan for stored ADAS-related codes. If warnings persist, perform radar/camera aiming and calibration, especially after windshield replacement, bumper repair, or alignment work. Replace the affected sensor only after confirming power, communication, and calibration status.
symptoms: ADAS warnings in rain or after car wash

communityRecommendations.content: Clean the radar emblem and the windshield area in front of the camera before assuming a failed sensor.
After windshield replacement, insist on proper camera calibration; many intermittent warnings trace back to skipped ADAS setup.

proposal.solution: Follow the owner warning message and current model-year repair information. before.title: Lower Ball Joint Wear or Separation Risk in Front Suspension
before.description: The first-generation IS shares a known Toyota/Lexus weakness involving front lower ball joints that can develop excessive play with age and mileage. Owners report clunking, wandering steering, uneven tire wear, and in severe cases joint separation that can cause loss of control. This is a heavily documented maintenance and safety concern in the IS300 community.
before.solution: Inspect front lower ball joints for play during any suspension or brake service, especially on higher-mileage cars or vehicles with unknown history. Replace worn joints promptly with OEM-quality parts and inspect adjacent components such as tie rods, control arm bushings, and front tires for secondary damage. An alignment should follow replacement.
symptoms: sudden wheel angle change if joint fails

communityRecommendations.content: Owners strongly recommend genuine Toyota/Lexus lower ball joints rather than cheap aftermarket units because failure consequences are severe.
If buying a used IS300, inspect lower ball joints immediately and budget for replacement if service history is unknown.

before.title: Premature Front Brake Squeal / Groan at Low Speed
before.description: A number of owners report front brake squeal, chirp, or groaning noises during light stops, especially when cold, damp, or after the vehicle sits overnight. This is commonly tied to pad material characteristics, rotor surface condition, or insufficient lubrication at pad contact points rather than outright brake failure. The complaint is more of a refinement issue, but it is frequent enough on owner forums and dealer visits to be considered a known nuisance.
before.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor finish, and hardware condition first. Dealers or independent shops typically clean and lubricate pad ears/shims, resurface or replace rotors if glazing is present, and install revised pads or shims if available. If the vehicle has F SPORT brakes, verify correct pad compound and bedding procedure after service.
symptoms: Groan when stopping at parking lot speeds
Noise worse when brakes are cold or damp
Brake noise without noticeable loss of stopping power

communityRecommendations.content: Ask for pad/rotor inspection before replacing parts; many cases improve with proper shim lubrication and pad bedding.
If replacing pads, use OEM or a known low-noise ceramic compound to preserve Lexus-level refinement.

proposal.solution: Have the brakes inspected for lining thickness, rotor condition, hardware, contamination and any safety fault before treating the noise as a refinement issue. before.title: 8-Speed Automatic Harsh Shifting
before.description: The Aisin 8-speed automatic transmission in the third-generation IS exhibits harsh or jerky shifts, particularly during low-speed 1-2 and 2-3 upshifts and when downshifting for deceleration. The transmission control module programming prioritizes fuel economy over smoothness, leading to abrupt gear changes that are felt prominently in the cabin.
before.solution: Visit the dealer for a transmission ECU reprogramming that smooths shift points and torque converter lockup behavior. Perform a transmission fluid drain-and-fill with Toyota WS fluid every 40,000 miles. If harsh shifting persists after the reflash, the valve body may need replacement.
symptoms: Hard jerk during 1-2 upshift at low speed
Transmission hesitation when accelerating from a stop

citations.title: Lexus TSB L-SB-0087-18 — IS transmission shift quality improvement reprogramming

communityRecommendations.content: A fluid drain-and-fill with genuine Toyota WS ATF makes a noticeable difference in shift quality. Do not flush — just drain and refill 4-5 quarts.

before.title: Valve Cover Gasket Leaks Causing Oil Smell and Misfire Risk
before.description: Aging valve cover gaskets on the 2JZ-GE commonly harden and leak, allowing oil to seep onto the cylinder head, spark plug tube seals, and exhaust side of the engine. Owners often notice a burnt-oil smell, visible oil around the valve covers, and occasional misfires if oil contaminates ignition components. This is one of the most common age-related engine leaks on the first-gen IS300.
before.solution: Confirm the leak source by cleaning the engine and inspecting around the valve cover perimeter and spark plug wells. Replace both valve cover gaskets, spark plug tube seals, and related grommets; many owners also replace the PCV valve at the same time to reduce crankcase pressure. If misfires are present, inspect and replace oil-soaked coil boots or plugs.

citations.title: My.IS and ClubLexus threads on IS300 valve cover gasket oil leaks

communityRecommendations.content: Use OEM valve cover gasket sets and replace spark plug tube seals and grommets at the same time to avoid repeat labor.
A PCV valve replacement is cheap preventive maintenance when doing this job.

proposal.solution: Clean and trace the oil source before removing components, then inspect the exact leak path and any ignition contamination under model-specific Lexus service information. Replace only confirmed leaking seals or damaged ignition components; do not bundle a PCV valve, plugs or coil boots from this page. This is a vehicle-specific diagnostic/service remedy; no universal retail part is asserted.
